core_obligations: Reduce to the case in which a suitable maximal minor of the matrix is invertible (proof lines 3843-3860).
Diagonalise the matrix by invertible row and column operations (proof lines 3860-3875).
Verify exactness in length one for the diagonal matrix by computing the kernel explicitly (proof lines 3875-3890).
Conclude the general case by localising where the minors become units (proof lines 3890-3896).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to an invertible minor (proof lines 3843-3860).
Read off exactness for the diagonal form and conclude by localisation (proof lines 3875-3896).
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a criterion for exactness in length one of a complex built from a matrix, phrased through the invertibility of a maximal minor, and the proof is a 54-line argument. It treats the case of an invertible maximal minor by an explicit change of bases that diagonalises the matrix and then reads the kernel off the diagonal form, and it reduces the general case to that one by localising at the primes where the relevant minors become units. Both the basis change and the exactness verification after it are displayed.
